claim.quote: We detect a muon with an estimated energy of 120 petaelectronvolts (PeV)

date.note: Publication year per the Nature journal reference. The event itself was recorded 2023-02-13; the Collaboration's own announcement is dated 2025-02-12.

key_value.locator: The observation of an ultra-high-energy cosmic neutrino at the bottom of the sea (km3net.org)
key_value.note: The Collaboration's own announcement pages give the event's estimated neutrino energy as ~220 PeV; the peer-reviewed abstract (INSPIRE) instead reports the reconstructed muon energy of 120 PeV, from which the higher neutrino energy is inferred. Both figures are recorded (muon energy in key_value_text) to avoid conflating the two.
key_value.quote: the neutrino's energy was estimated to be an astonishing 220 peta-electronvolts (PeV)

key_value_text.locator: The observation of an ultra-high-energy cosmic neutrino at the bottom of the sea (km3net.org)
key_value_text.quote: On February 13, 2023, the KM3NeT team recorded a neutrino event unlike any other.
key_value_text.value: Estimated cosmic-neutrino energy ~220 PeV (Collaboration announcement); reconstructed muon energy 120 PeV (paper abstract). Near-horizontal muon track detected by KM3NeT/ARCA on 2023-02-13, event designated KM3-230213A.

name: Observation of an ultra-high-energy cosmic neutrino with KM3NeT
notes: This is the mandatory flagship result specified in the brief (the KM3-230213A event). result_type set to 'observation' per the A16 mechanical check: the paper title contains 'Observation'.

Journal page numbers (376-382) and volume/issue (638/8050) were obtained via the INSPIRE literature API (record 2879193) fetched this session, not by directly reading the paywalled nature.com article (WebFetch of nature.com redirected to an authentication wall).

significance.locator: INSPIRE literature record 2879193 / Nature 638, 376-382 (2025), abstract (no sigma-level significance reported)
significance.note: No sigma-level significance is reported for this single-event observation in the abstract text obtained; the reported quantity is the estimated muon/neutrino energy, not a discovery significance.

summary.plain: KM3NeT's ARCA telescope caught the most energetic neutrino ever recorded, a near-horizontal flash of light from a particle interaction on the sea floor in February 2023, suggesting an origin far more powerful than any neutrino source seen before.
summary.technical: Single ultra-high-energy through-going muon event (KM3-230213A), recorded 2023-02-13 by 21 active KM3NeT/ARCA detection units, with reconstructed muon energy 120 PeV implying a still higher parent-neutrino energy (~220 PeV, Collaboration estimate); the highest-energy neutrino candidate reported to date, published in Nature 638, 376-382 (2025).

title: Observation of an ultra-high-energy cosmic neutrino with KM3NeT
why_it_matters: The event's energy far exceeds any previously detected neutrino, implying either a new class of cosmic accelerator or the first detection of a cosmogenic neutrino produced by ultra-high-energy cosmic rays interacting with the cosmic microwave background.
